newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Taylors sees "satisfactory" full year.
newsitem.headline: Taylors sees "satisfactory" full year.

text.p: Laundry firm Taylors Group Ltd said on Monday it expected a "satisfactory" full year result but would not sustain first-half profit growth which was influenced by acquisitions.
Taylors earlier reported a rise in net profit for the six months to December 31 to NZ$1.22 million from $788,000 a year earlier. Revenue was up 19.3 percent at $16.7 million.
The result included trading by Wairoa Textiles, which commenced in June 1996 and provides linen services to Health Waikato.
"Sales and profits from this new business were close to budget expectations," Taylors said.
It said the normally stable healthcare sector of the market had experienced some uncertainty over government funding and not all of this had been resolved.

"Shifts in the inward tourist pattern have continued. Hospitality sales in Auckland have been strong, but in spite of strong new business development, have struggled elsewhere to keep pace with last year," it said.

"The entry into the Rotorua market through the Lakeland Hospital Laundry offers an opportunity for further growth in the local hospitality market. While opportunities for expansion in the healthcare market continue to be pursued, it is unlikely that outcomes from this source will impact the second half results."
In hospitality, softer trading conditions in the South Island would dampen the effects of improving trading conditions in Auckland.

"While the profit performance growth rate achieved in the first half, which was influenced by acquisition, will not be maintained, it is expected that given continuity of existing markets conditions, a satisfactory result for the full year will be achieved." -- Wellington newsroom 64 4 473-4746
